about: The zero-knowledge pass's baseline (packages/editor/ARCHITECTURE.md, *What's self-explanatory*): per feature, the pass's questions answered by an agent from the code alone (comments blanked, no docs: .refs/full-editor~stripped/) and from the code as it is (comments, still no Markdown or .silo/: .refs/full-editor/), through the editor's files_read, files_glob and files_grep — graded against the key (the manifest's what and ways, the ledger, the docs): 1 right, 0.5 partly right or right but guessed, 0 wrong. A feature's pass runs again when it's reintroduced, against this.

features.feature: Answer a call where it stops

questions.asked: What does it do, for a person using the editor?
questions.key: A run reaching a call that touches files, the network or commands that nothing has decided stops on that line and asks in the margin: allow, skip or deny, for this call, this run or always, or make a rule.
command editor.capability.decide; the Margin's margin.decide and margin.rule; a debug adapter tracker; hub request debug.session.<id>.decide.

questions.asked: Besides capability-stops.ts, which files are part of it?
questions.key: The debugger's side: tsval's adapter and worker handling `decide` (split into adapter/stops.ts and worker/stops.ts since).

questions.asked: Why does "for this run" cover every call of the capability, not only calls reaching the same resource?
questions.key: A loop's calls reach a different resource each time round (capability-stops.ts 119–120, a comment).

code alone.said: inferred: a resource often isn't known before the call; a rule on one resource wouldn't match non-literal arguments

questions.key: capability-stops.ts and its registration; the Margin's ask item and commands; the debugger's decide; policyFor's and takeOnce's other callers (debug-events.ts, runtime-fs.ts) need another source.

as it is.said: more than the key: runs_tests' approvals send allow-once

questions.asked: What does it do, and for whom?
questions.key: An agent notes the working tree, tries a change, sees what it breaks, and puts every file back if it doesn't hold; and previews a replacement across files as a diff before making it.

as it is.said: the undo half; the preview half only as files_replace's pointer

questions.key: agent tools workspace_checkpoint and workspace_restore; hub requests workspace.checkpoint and workspace.restore; core module installCheckpoints.

questions.asked: Besides checkpoints.ts, which code is part of it?
questions.key: app/tools/workspace/tools.ts, the install in workbench-entry.tsx, its test.

questions.asked: Why does a checkpoint leave out .silo/?
questions.key: The editor keeps its records there as it goes (the baseline, pinned versions): a restore would undo the editor's work, not the agent's (the header comment).

code alone.said: right, from the agent tool's description string, held as an inference

questions.key: checkpoints.ts, the workspace tool family, the install, its test and page-tools' names; files_replace's description points at it.

questions.asked: What does it do, for a person using the editor?
questions.key: A note attached to a piece of code follows that code as it moves and changes; when the code is gone, the note waits in Problems to be re-placed or dismissed.
commands notes.add, confirm, dismiss, placeHere, replace; the comment controller; the notes diagnostics and code actions; a status bar item; agent tool notes_add and hub request notes.add.

questions.asked: Where does a note's place in the code come from: what does it rely on, through what?
questions.key: Annotations that stay on their code: the editor's BABLR, through the bridge's editor.annotations.refer and resolve (hub annotations.*).

questions.asked: Why does dismissing a note write it back marked dismissed, rather than deleting it?
questions.key: So a branch merge can't bring the note back (the header comment; notes merge line by line).

code alone.said: the same reason, inferred from the merge rule, low confidence: 'I couldn't find the reason stated'

questions.key: extensions/notes, its bundledExtension, notes_add and the notes.add hub request; its tests; the annotations commands stay (others use them).

code alone.said: no tests or other callers: greps across folders timed out
